article:
A date is a feature

Shipped means a stranger can find it without you sitting next to them. A URL. A post. A film. A date on the tape. Private polish is a way to never be seen. Ugly in public is a way to get the next error from someone who is not you.

X is the short cut and the conversation. YouTube is the lesson that still exists next month. This site is the house they walk back to. All three, same day, same claim. Not a content calendar. A habit.

What to post

The thing that existed this morning and exists now. A screen. One sentence a noob can repeat. A link. You can talk about Grok without doing an ad read. Show the work. The product is the proof.

@bohobond is a character. The posts should sound like the tape, not like a course landing page.

How I actually do it

The first twenty films are these chapters. Each one should leave a short cut on X and a long cut in the slot on the right. If the article is still a draft, the film can still go out — say it is a draft. People prefer a live draft to a perfect silence.

Where noobs get stuck

Waiting for the personal brand to be ready. Waiting for ten products. Waiting for permission. Or posting threads about building and never linking a URL.

Film this

The post going out. The YouTube upload. The chapter slot with the film in it. Then close the laptop. The point is that it exists without you watching it.

Do this before chapter 20

  • Pick a date for video 01. Put it on the tape.
  • Ship the short cut even if the long cut is rough.
  • Reply to one person who is earlier than you.
  • Do not build a funnel before you have a film.

Next: tiny business — invoices, a company if it happens. Code was the easy part.
